subject: forestSpirit
reasoning:
I'm designing a stylized forest spirit model—tall humanoid form with an antler/branch crown, mossy bark torso, glowing eyes, and flowing leaf-cape tendrils—using blocky primitives in a TypeScript SDK module, making sure I reference the API correctly as I plan the structure.

I'm working through uncertainty around the builder API: how joints get parented to each other, whether sweep/loft take radius as a number or function, and how ring callbacks are structured, so I'm choosing the most plausible interpretations and planning to lean on sweep rather than loft to reduce risk.

I'm also deciding to avoid uncertain paint/pattern functions in favor of flat colors, and to skip legs entirely by giving the spirit a tapering root-like base that sinks into the ground instead of relying on unclear IK/limb functions — this sidesteps several unknowns while still producing a coherent, self-contained design.

Now I'm sketching out the actual joint coordinates and chain structure: planning root/hip/spine/neck placement along the vertical axis, using chains for spine and antler branches, and spike primitives for tapered antler tines, all oriented so the model stands at roughly 2.2m tall facing forward.

For body geometry, I'm leaning toward a sweep along the spine path for the torso with bark-colored texture, a sphere for the pelvis, and a low-poly dodecahedron for the head to keep a stylized look, plus small glowing sphere eyes embedded in the face.

Figuring out eye placement...

Now I'm thinking through antlers—sprouting a limb-like joint chain from a point near the top of the head, defining the growth as a named joint with a tip and radius to form the horn shape.

Still shaping leaf geometry...

For scattering moss and leaves, I'm relying on surface.scatter(count) to place hits across the torso sweep, then sticking small flat stones or leaves onto those points, trusting it uses an internal seeded rng for determinism rather than passing one explicitly. I'm also picking out bark and moss material colors now.

For the limbs I'm building arm chains like armL through shoulder, elbow, and hand joints, then sweeping a thin radius tube along that path with a role tag like "arm" so the system knows how to treat those joints. For the torso I'm setting up a spine chain with role "spine" and sweeping it with a thicker radius, possibly adding a separate bulbous part for the chest.

Now I'm sketching out a cloak made from a membrane stretched between two hanging edge paths from the shoulders down to near the ground, trying to work out how color gets passed into that membrane call since the signature isn't fully certain yet.

Then I'm planning root-like tendrils flaring from the hips down into the ground, a glowing icosahedron orb held in one hand for a lantern effect, hair tendrils sweeping back from the head, and simple eye sockets and a carved mouth detail on the face, with the whole figure resting on the ground plane.

For the skeleton structure, I'm working out joint hierarchy—starting with a hips root joint, then chaining spine up through neck to head, and attaching arm chains with a parent reference so they connect properly to the torso rather than floating as separate roots.

I'll skip the separate hips joint and instead have the spine chain itself serve as the root, since the spec requires exactly one root joint without a parent, then parent other chains off the spine's base joint.

For the head and neck, I'll simplify by defining a neck chain running from chest to just below the head, then a standalone head joint parented to the neck's last joint, keeping geometry like a dodecahedron for the head shape.

For antlers and leaves, I'm sketching out a sprout-based approach: antler sprouts off a head surface point with a tip, extra spike tines for branching detail, and a scatter of leaf points stuck to the head surface for foliage.

For the face and accessories, I'm placing small glowing sphere eyes near the front of the head, skipping pupil detail, and adding a glowing icosahedron lantern near the hand. Then I'm defining hair tendrils as short sweeping chains trailing from the back of the head and simple root chains sweeping downward from the hips, keeping the structure minimal before finalizing all the named pieces.
